tech.name: Python
tech.meaning: Python is a simple, easy to read programming language. It is used for websites, automation, data analysis and AI.
tech.why: It is the easiest language to start with, and many college projects and jobs use it.
learn: Mini projects like a quiz app and a chatbot

tech.name: HTML, CSS & JavaScript
tech.meaning: HTML builds the structure of a web page, CSS styles it, and JavaScript makes it interactive. Together they power every website.
tech.why: You can build and publish a real website in a few weeks and show it to anyone.
learn: Flexbox, grid and mobile friendly design
Calling APIs and building a portfolio

tech.name: React
tech.meaning: React is a JavaScript library for building fast web apps from small, reusable pieces called components.
tech.why: It is one of the most asked skills for front end jobs and internships.

tech.name: Java
tech.meaning: Java is a strong, widely used programming language for apps, banking systems and Android development.
tech.why: It is part of most college syllabuses and is used by many big companies.

tech.name: SQL & MySQL
tech.meaning: SQL (Structured Query Language) is the language used to store, read and update data in a database. MySQL is a popular database that runs SQL.
tech.why: Almost every app stores data, so SQL is useful in every project and every interview.
learn: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY and GROUP BY
Designing a database for a mini project
tech.example:
SELECT name, marks
FROM students
WHERE marks > 80
ORDER BY marks DESC;

tech.name: Git & GitHub
tech.meaning: Git tracks the changes in your code. GitHub is a website where you store your code and share it with others.
tech.why: Recruiters check your GitHub profile. It also lets you publish websites for free.
learn: Working with others using pull requests
Publishing a site with GitHub Pages
tech.example:
git add .
git commit -m "First commit"
git push origin main

tech.name: Data Structures
tech.meaning: Data structures are ways to organise data, like arrays, stacks, trees and graphs, so programs can work with it quickly.
tech.why: They are the base of coding interviews and help you write faster, cleaner programs.
learn: Arrays, linked lists, stacks and queues

tech.name: Machine Learning
tech.meaning: Machine learning lets a computer learn patterns from data and make predictions, like suggesting a movie or spotting spam.
tech.why: It is a fast growing field and makes a great final year project.
learn: Checking how good a model is
tech.example:
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
model = LinearRegression().fit(X, y)
print(model.predict([[5]]))

project.name: Student Management System
project.desc: Add, search and manage student records.
project.overview: A desktop style app that stores student details, marks and attendance in a MySQL database. It is simple to explain in a viva and easy to extend.
features: Search by name or roll number

project.name: E-commerce Website
project.desc: Product pages, cart and checkout flow.
project.overview: A responsive online shop with product listing, cart and a checkout form. A strong choice for a final year project.
features: Add to cart and update quantity

project.name: Chatbot using Python
project.desc: A simple AI chatbot with viva notes.
project.overview: A chatbot that understands basic questions and replies using simple natural language processing.

project.name: Portfolio Website Starter
project.desc: A free template to build your own portfolio.
project.overview: A clean one page portfolio template. Replace the text and images and publish it for free on GitHub Pages.

post.title: Do not compare your day one with someone's day 100
post.summary: A reminder for every student who feels behind.
body: Everyone starts somewhere. The person you admire also wrote bad code, failed tests and felt lost.
Keep showing up. Small progress every day closes the gap faster than you think.

post.title: Your marks are not your skills
post.summary: Practice and projects speak louder than a score.
body: Companies look for people who can build and learn. A good project shows that better than a number.
Spend this week building one small thing. Then show it to someone.

post.title: When you feel like quitting
post.summary: Rest, then try one tiny step.
body: Feeling stuck is part of learning, not a sign that you are not good enough.
Take a break. Come back and solve just one small part of the problem.

post.title: How to choose your final year project
post.summary: Pick an idea that is doable and impressive.
body: Choose a problem you understand, like attendance, billing or a study planner.
Start with a small working version, then add features one by one.
Make sure you can explain every line of your code in your viva.

post.title: Roadmap to become a web developer
post.summary: What to learn first, next and last.
body: Start with HTML and CSS. Then learn JavaScript.
Build three small projects. Then learn a framework like React.
Put everything on GitHub and share your portfolio link.

post.title: How to learn programming without feeling lost
post.summary: A simple weekly plan for beginners.
body: Learn one concept, then build something tiny with it.
Repeat every week. Small projects add up fast.

post.title: Why I started iterawin
post.summary: The idea behind this page and what you can expect.
body: I want every student to have a clear path from learning to a real project to a job.
Follow along. New posts, videos and projects arrive often.
